'''John Ernst Freund''' (August 6, 1921 – August 14, 2004) was a prominent author of university level textbooks on [[statistics]] and a mathematics professor at [[Arizona State University]]. Born in Berlin, Germany, he emigrated to [[Mandatory Palestine]] in the 1930s. He studied at the [[University of London]] and at the [[University of California at Los Angeles]], from which he received his bachelor's degree. He did graduate work at [[Columbia University]] and the [[University of Pittsburgh]], from which he received his doctorate in 1952.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Goodall |first=Gerald |date=January 13, 2005 |title=News and Notes |journal=Teaching Statistics |volume=27 |issue=1 |page=32 |doi=10.1111/j.1467-9639.2005.00201.x}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam Archive |publisher=Mathematical Association of America |date=December 31, 2009 |url=https://www.maa.org/news/memoriam-archive }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=John Ernst Freund |work=The Arizona Republic |date=August 18, 2004 |url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/azcentral/obituary.aspx?n=john-ernst-freund&pid=2526788 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3yZMAAAAMAAJ |last=Freund |first=John E. |date=1971 |title=Mathematical statistics |publisher=Prentice-Hall|isbn=9780135622230 }} See "About the Author".</ref>

In 1960 he was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx |title=Fellows of the ASA |publisher=American Statistical Association |access-date=2022-02-04}} Entry for Freund, John. E</ref>
